_description: Per-kind structural checklists used by /projectstore:review. Each kind defines `default_review` (whether peer-reviewer skill auto-suggests review after creation) and an `items` array fed verbatim to the critic agent.

items: Decision section is unambiguous — a stranger could implement it from this file alone, with no other context.
At least one named Alternative is present with an explicit rejection reason ('Rejected because: ...').
Consequences include at least one Negative / trade-off stated honestly. Reject sales framing.
All hand-wavy referents ('we', 'users', 'the system') are resolved to concrete actors or components.
No marketing language: 'blazingly', 'robust', 'best-in-class', 'magnificent', 'rock-solid', etc.
Context explains why the decision is needed NOW (vs. a year ago or in 6 months).
References cite at least one external doc / prior ADR / RFC if relevant.
Status, Date, Authors metadata filled (not template placeholders).
No TODOs, no '...', no empty bullets in the final body.
Question is sharp — answerable by yes/no/comparison, not 'tell me about X'.
TL;DR is a single paragraph that gives the conclusion before the body.
Method describes how findings were gathered (docs read, benchmarks run, experts asked) — not just 'I researched'.
Comparison table has populated Pros AND Cons cells; empty cells flagged.
Conclusion explicitly ties back to the original Question. Recommendation is actionable.
References are linkable (URL / file path), not 'see [some doc]'.
No unstated benchmarks ('it's faster' without numbers).
Findings are evidence-based, not opinion. Where opinion appears, it's labelled.
How we solve references at least one ADR by id; the references resolve.
Behavioral contracts are numbered and individually testable — each states an observable outcome, not an implementation step.
Acceptance items are checkboxes; acceptance is explicitly ADDITIVE to the covered stories' own criteria, not a replacement.
Acceptance items that belong to specific stories carry a '— stories: <id>' attribution; items meant for all covered stories are unattributed on purpose.
frontmatter stories: uses <epic-id>/<story-id> path form, inline flow list.
Mandatory sections present (How we solve / Behavioral contracts / Acceptance); Modules-on-disk and Testing may be omitted only for research spikes.
For a spike spec: contracts read as questions-to-answer plus exit criteria.
No TODOs, no '...', no empty bullets in the final body.
Goal is measurable — success can be verified, not just described.
Context explains why this epic exists and which downstream pieces depend on it.
Stories table has at least 2 entries; first story description is concrete enough to start.
Expected Results contains testable outcomes, not aspirations.
Dependencies list external blockers (people, systems, decisions), not just sibling stories.
Open Questions are real unknowns, not rhetorical filler.
Priority assigned (p0 / p1 / p2), not left as default if epic is non-trivial.
Description states the user/actor and the value of the change.
Decomposition checklist has items granular enough to finish in a session each.
Acceptance Criteria are testable (someone could write tests from these).
Technical Notes flag any non-obvious risks or constraints.
Definition fits in one paragraph; a stranger leaves knowing what the concept IS.
Examples ground the concept (at least one concrete case).
Attendees listed.
Decisions section captures what was actually decided (not just discussed).
Action items have an owner.
Purpose states WHEN to run this runbook (trigger conditions).
Prerequisites are listable checks, not prose.
Verification step exists and is testable.
Rollback step exists for any irreversible action.
